title: Vocabulary & Language
subject: Bahasa Inggris
prerequisites: Peserta didik telah memiliki pengetahuan dasar untuk menyebutkan nama-nama pakaian yang dikenakan sehari-hari.
resources: Sumber Belajar:  Rise Up! Teens! Student Book 1, page 48-50
Laptop/ komputer, pengeras suara, projector, PPT
learningModel: Discovery Learning, Task-Based Learning, Tatap Muka.
approach: Peserta didik diajak untuk fokus dan saksama saat menyimak audio, mengamati detail gambar/komik, dan memperhatikan struktur bahasa yang digunakan.
Peserta didik menghubungkan materi pembelajaran dengan pengalaman dan kehidupan nyata mereka, sehingga pembelajaran terasa relevan dan bermanfaat.
Pembelajaran dikemas dalam aktivitas yang menyenangkan seperti permainan tebak hobi, kerja kelompok, penggunaan komik strip, dan survei interaktif.
objectives: Learners will learn new words about clothing and how to describe it by size, colour, and pattern.
Learners will be able to understand, identify, and say key vocabulary about clothing.
Learners will be able to ask and answer questions about the cost of clothes.

details: Greet the students and ask about their feelings. For example: “How are you feeling today?” or “How would you describe your mood in one word?”
The teacher introduces himself/herself in front of the class.
Get to know the students by using the letter game.
The teacher writes down his/her name on the board (e.g. Susan)
Ask the student if their name starts with the shown letter (e.g. starts with S) and then they must stand up and introduce themselves. Continue with other letters.
Other alternatives to get to know the students: hot potato and throw the ball.
Ask students to look at the pictures and questions on page 48.

Put students into groups of 3-4 and ask them to talk about what they can see in the pictures. Tell them to write down any English words they know about clothes in their notebooks. Elicit some ideas and write the key words on the board.
Read the questions together and model your own answers first, e.g. “At school I wear a uniform. At home I wear comfortable clothes.”
Tell students they have 5-6 minutes to discuss the questions. Encourage them to use English, but if they don’t have enough vocabulary, it’s acceptable to use some words in their first language.
After 5-6 minutes, stop the task and elicit some ideas from students (e.g. “Clothes can be new or old, big or small.”).
Tell students not to worry if the questions were difficult. By the end of this unit they will be able to describe clothes, say why clothes are suitable or not, and ask how much clothes cost.
Ask students to look at Student Book page 49 and ask the class, “What can you see on the page?”
Tell students that they will do a listening task. They need to listen and write the number in each box according to the order they hear the words in the audio.
Before playing the audio, read all of the words together: a checked hoodie, a school uniform, a spotted umbrella, big shoes, a yellow jacket, small clothes, a loose T-shirt, comfortable pants.
Play audio 6.1. If needed, the teacher can pause the audio after track 1 to check that the students understand how to do the task. Then, continue with the audio.
Ask students to check their answers with a partner, then play the audio again.
Check the answers together. Write the correct answers on the board or show them on the screen using the PPT for this book.
Ask students to read the sentences from the audio script aloud, in pairs (e.g. “I am wearing a yellow jacket today because it is cold outside.”).
This activity is for pronunciation practice.
Tell students to listen and repeat the words they hear.
Play audio 6.2 and encourage students to repeat the words loudly, and encourage them to try to copy the intonation they hear in the audio. Check that all students are repeating the vocabulary.
Pay attention to the pronunciation of “checked”, “spotted”, “loose”, and “comfortable”.
For variation, vocabulary drilling can be done in groups, pairs, loudly, quietly, etc.
Ask students to look in their books at the Vocabulary C task on page 49 and check if students understand the task, e.g., Which activity are we doing? What page is it on? What do you have to do?
Tell students to look at each picture carefully and complete the sentences with a describing word and a clothing item (e.g. school uniform, loose T-shirt, checked jacket, spotted umbrella).
Do the first number together as a class to make sure students understand what to do.
Put students in pairs and ask them to complete the task in around 7 minutes.

Then, check the answers. Write the answers on the board or show them on the screen using the PPT for this book. Accept other suitable describing words where the picture allows (e.g. a loose OR blue T-shirt).
Ask students to read the completed sentences aloud to each other, in pairs.
This is an additional activity for further practice if there is time.
Put students in pairs. Ask them to look at the words and pictures in Vocabulary A.

Ask them to write one question for each word (eight questions in total), or choose four words and write four questions, e.g. “Do you have a checked hoodie?”, “What color is your school uniform?”, “Do you like comfortable pants?”
Give around 5 minutes to do this. Elicit some questions from the class and give corrective feedback if the questions have mistakes.
Then, ask pairs to sit with another pair to make groups of four, and take turns asking and answering their questions.
After around 5 minutes, ask some groups to share their questions and answers with the class.
Ask students to open their Student Book to page 50.
First, the teacher reads the Q&A models in the speech bubbles at the top of the page aloud for the students to hear.
Next, the teacher asks everyone to read the Q&A models aloud as a class.
Then, the teacher asks students to read the Q&A models together in pairs (Read with a friend).

Write the patterns on the board: “How much does the jacket cost? – The jacket costs $24.99.” and “How much do the shoes cost? – The shoes cost $12.99.” Highlight: does + one item, do + two or more items (pants, shoes, socks); costs in the answer for one item.

This can be repeated several times by putting students into different pairs. Encourage students to change the key vocabulary in the questions and answers, by using the vocabulary learned on the previous page.

Check the Teacher’s Guide to see further explanation about the Language Box (meaning, form, use, common mistakes), e.g. “How much does it costs?” and “How much do the jacket cost?” are common mistakes.
Ask students to look at the practice task B on Student Book page 50.

Explain that they need to unscramble the words to make correct questions and answers. Highlight that for some numbers they unscramble the question, and for others they unscramble the answer. Remind students to use the Q&A models and the Language Box on the page.
Put students in pairs and give them around 6-8 minutes to complete the task.
Ask students to check their answers with a new partner, then elicit the answers and write them on the board (e.g. “The spotted T-shirt costs $9.99.” / “How much do the big shoes cost?”).
Ask students to correct their answers if they are wrong.
Then, Student A asks the questions and Student B answers them. After that, they switch roles.
To make the checking answer stage more fun, teachers could let the students choose their own classmates to answer the next question by passing a marker or tossing a paper ball.
This is an additional activity for further practice if there is time.

Put students in pairs. Ask students to write four questions for their partner about how much different things cost. They can ask about the clothes they are wearing, or objects they have with them at school.
Tell students they don’t need to give the real cost. They can say any price they want, and they can be funny or creative, but they can’t say “I don’t know.”
Write the following on the board to guide students:
A: How much do your shoes cost?
B: My shoes cost 35 dollars. / My shoes cost 1,000 dollars!
A: How much does your school bag cost?
B: My school bag costs 20 dollars.
Remind students to use does/costs for one item and do/cost for plural items.
Elicit some of the funniest questions and answers from the class.
Choose 1-2 students to describe one item of clothing they are wearing today (size, colour, or pattern) and ask a friend how much it costs.
Conclude the lesson, give feedback, and appreciation toward the student(s) / the whole class. Dismiss the class.

assessment: Asesmen formatif: pengamatan pelafalan saat drill kosakata (listen and repeat).
Pemeriksaan jawaban latihan kosakata dan language practice di Student Book.
Unjuk kerja lisan: peserta didik memakai kosakata & struktur baru dalam kalimat sendiri.
reflectionStudent: Apa hal baru yang kamu pelajari hari ini?
Bagian mana yang paling mudah dan paling sulit bagimu? Mengapa?
Kalimat bahasa Inggris apa yang sudah bisa kamu ucapkan dengan percaya diri?
Apa yang akan kamu lakukan untuk berlatih di rumah?
reflectionTeacher: Apakah tujuan pembelajaran tercapai? Bukti apa yang menunjukkannya?
Kegiatan mana yang paling efektif dan mana yang perlu diperbaiki?
Berapa persen instruksi kelas yang disampaikan dalam bahasa Inggris?
Peserta didik mana yang memerlukan pendampingan atau pengayaan?
